o1.biggest_strength: It rebuilds the flow around the data's three signals (pause for 'no time', annual switch for monthly 'too expensive', reminder for 'not progressing') and shows the money with honest assumptions.
o1.biggest_mistake: It keeps a 50% discount for the 'switching apps' group with no evidence it works, and its own maths shows that group returns only about 67 people; the 'too expensive, monthly' cancelling count (3,379) is inconsistent with the stated 64% of 5,280 (3,379), which the owner notes give as a fact but the arithmetic there is shaky.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Drop the untested discount for switchers, align the segment counts exactly with 64% of 5,280, and present a single clean first-week build order.

o2.biggest_strength: It is disciplined: no discount anywhere, the pause is front and centre, every number traces cleanly to the brief, and it ends with a measurement plan and pre-launch confirmations the team can act on.
o2.biggest_mistake: It offers nothing to the 'switching apps' group, which is a defensible but slightly under-explored choice; the owner might have wanted at least a reason to test a competitor save.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: A short test plan for the 'switching apps' segment and a one-line note on why a clean exit beats a competitor discount there.

reason: Both bring the pause back and kill the blanket discount, but Output 2 is cleaner on the money, avoids untested discounts entirely, and its numbers reconcile exactly to the brief, so I'd hand it to the product team as is.
